newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SWIMMING-HEYNS PULLS OUT OF 200 METRES AHEAD OF GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-HEYNS PULLS OUT OF 200 METRES AHEAD OF GAMES.

text.p: Olympic double gold medallist Penny Heyns pulled out of her 200-metre breaststroke heat at the South African national swimming championships on Friday, having already qualified for August's Pan-Pacific Games.
The 22-year-old had hinted after her 100-metre breastroke victory on Thursday evening that she was not keen on swimming in the 200 metres because she returned to training only on January 15.

"I made a telephone call to my former university coach Jan Bidrman in Canada earlier today and he suggested that, since the Japanese swimming federation have already invited me to compete in the Pan-Pacific Games, I did not have to swim the 200 metres to qualify," Heyns told Reuters.
"Anybody who saw me swim last year will know that my stroke has not been great this week. I return to the U.S. next week and I want to go back in a positive frame of mind about my swimming."
In the absence of Heyns, her University of Nebraska team mate Julia Russell produced a Pan-Pacific qualifying time of two minutes 35.93 seconds in the morning heats of the 200-metre breaststroke.
Russell then won the evening final with a time of 2:36.51.
